correctness.rationale: The exact nth iterate of the affine Jordan shear has last-coordinate obstruction n*a_d=0 modulo one. Conditional on that obstruction, its (d-1) remaining equations are an upper triangular integral torus endomorphism with diagonal n, so there are n^(d-1) discrete solutions and one free circle coordinate. Least period is constant along each circle, justifying Möbius inversion; the Jordan product, dimension threshold, and the rational power-sum generating function yield the full claim. The saved standalone checker independently enumerates 4092 exact rational fixed-circle representatives over 36 cases and validates 380 generating coefficients, corroborating but not replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The specific new statement is a complete count of every exact-period circle component for one integral unipotent Jordan block with arbitrary affine translation, the sharp dimension-two versus higher-dimensional primitive share, and the evaluated essential-singularity component-zeta. The recent primary-MSC 37E45 toral dynamics paper addresses polynomial entropy under a homotopy-to-identity assumption, not the present Jordan shears; the recent published unipotent-Jordan Bowen-ball result treats the same map but a different invariant. The supporting 2026 affine-torus paper addresses reversibility, entropy and ordinary fixed points, not all-iterate component counts. The classical handbook motivates component counts and proves polynomial-entropy properties but does not evaluate the claimed Jordan-totient or component-zeta formulas. Byszewski–Graff–Ward treat the usual finite periodic-point count framework. Two closely related prior research results were read in full: a unipotent shear Bowen-ball volume formula, and a cat-driven Möbius period-two identity-fiber resonance; neither statement implies the new all-period arithmetic census. Standard determinant, Möbius, and Euler-product tools are acknowledged. Residual priority risks are explicit.
residual_risks: A general but unidentified result in Nielsen periodic-point theory, algebraic dynamics or torus skew shifts could subsume these explicit computations.
The Jordan-totient factor and Euler product are standard arithmetic facts; novelty, if any, lies in the evaluated all-period component classification and its dynamical zeta, not in those facts.
No independent publication-priority or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The standard connected-component periodic invariant is motivated by nonisolated families. The theorem completely classifies that invariant for the canonical affine parabolic Jordan map in all dimensions, makes the exact primitive fraction explicit, discovers a qualitative dimension-two versus higher-dimensional positive-density boundary, and evaluates a component-zeta with essential singularities despite zero entropy. It does not claim that the standard Jordan totient, lattice-index, or general component-count framework is new.
